Blocked-by: #10921

Why blocked rather than queued: this card and #10921 both stall on **one prior fact** — whether these out-of-repo `@objectstack/` names ship anywhere, and where that is recorded. The body says so itself ("Answer the prior question first"). #10921 is now the parent carrying that question into the decision inbox; grading this one separately would put the same question in front of the maintainer twice, which the same-family meta-criterion forbids.

⚠️ Unlock is **not automatic** and the scan will not find it: #10921 is a decision card, so it stays open after it is ruled on. Its ruling comment carries an explicit 裁后执行段 clearing this card's `pm:blocked` in the same write. If you are reading this card and #10921 has been ruled, that clearing is the step that was owed — do it rather than waiting.

Routing correction, from the anchoring rule: re-labelled `domain:devx` → **`domain:services`**. The fix lands in `packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/knowledge.manifest.ts` — both the adapter-list comment and the runtime validation message, which is the sharp half (it is spoken to an operator inside Settings → AI & Embedder). The `domain:devx` label the filer applied belongs to the sweep this was found in (#10893), not to where the repair lands.

⛔ Scope fence for whoever takes it: the `packages/spec/src/contracts/embedder.ts` half (the `IEmbedder` docblock naming the two absent adapters) is **not in this card**. `packages/spec` has exactly one owner and it is not this lane. If the ruling on #10921 turns out to require both halves in one PR, come back to triage for a cross-domain designation rather than reaching into spec from here — or the spec half gets its own card with a `Blocked-by:` of its own. Note the spec half also carries the ADR-0049 question the body raises (`IEmbedder` has no in-repo consumer at all), which is a heavier question than a docblock edit and is another reason not to ride it along.

## Review — PR #11319 · substance **ACCEPT** · ⛔ flip deferred (CI still converging)

### ⚠️ First, on the record: my dispatch's fork clause was wrong, and the dev was right to refuse it

My claim comment (`5385454896`) offered the dev a two-way fork. The second branch read:

> **The roster is present and does NOT name it** → you also have the prior fact, and it says the package ships nowhere → the repair is to drop the `turso` adapter option and the claim.

That clause is **defective**, and following it mechanically would have deleted a working, published adapter from the settings surface. The dev measured instead of obeying, and found the third case my fork did not contain: `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` **is** present on the ref (PR #11266 merged as `a2ec377078`), but it is keyed by `requires:` platform *service* capability tokens and contains **no knowledge adapter at all** — not `knowledge-turso`, and not the two this repo does build. Its silence is **category silence**, not a negative answer.

I wrote "absent from the roster ⇒ ships nowhere" into a dispatch. That inference does not hold against a roster that was never in the business of listing knowledge adapters, and the failure mode it would have produced — a silent deletion justified by a lookup in the wrong table — is worse than the defect the card was filed about. The triage unlock condition (`5385332333`) pointed at that roster as the way to answer the question, so the premise is partly inherited, but the fork clause was mine. **Zone-2 assumptions exist to be falsified and this one was; recording it rather than quietly benefiting from the dev's better judgement.**

### Independent verification of the load-bearing facts

The repair's whole direction rests on "it IS published", and the PR writes a version claim into **operator-facing product text**, so I re-measured rather than accepting the report. Same registry, unauthenticated, today:

| claim in the PR | my independent measurement | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `knowledge-turso` published, `latest` 6.9.0 | HTTP 200, `latest` = **6.9.0** | ✅ |
| published 2026-05-27 | `time["6.9.0"]` = **2026-05-27T14:14:24Z** | ✅ |
| nine versions from 6.4.0 | **9** versions, earliest **6.4.0** | ✅ |
| 6.9.0 **exact-pins** `@objectstack/spec@6.9.0` | `dependencies["@objectstack/spec"]` = **`6.9.0`** — exact, no caret (also `core` and `service-knowledge` at `6.9.0`) | ✅ |
| this repo ships 17.2.0 | `@objectstack/spec` `latest` = **17.2.0** | ✅ |
| `knowledge-sqlite-vec` 404 (negative control) | **404** | ✅ |
| `security-enterprise` 404 (known-private control) | **404** | ✅ |

Every factual claim confirmed. The control discipline is right in both directions — positive controls prove the probe works, the known-private 404 proves a 404 means "not on the public registry" rather than "probe broken", and the zero-hit `ls-tree` carries its own reverse control (`knowledge-memory` and `knowledge-ragflow` at 8 each under the identical command shape).

### What the measurement added that neither branch anticipated

The package is published **and not co-installable with this platform version**. Mounting it resolves a second `@objectstack/spec` (6.9.0) alongside this one (17.2.0). An operator told only "mount it" walks straight into that — so the original message was not merely unfollowable, it was unfollowable in a way that would have produced a confusing dependency failure rather than a clean "not found". The new message carries its own version boundary instead of just its package name. That is a better repair than either branch I described.

### The diff

Three files, all on-scope: the manifest, its test, and a changeset. `packages/spec` untouched — the scope fence holds. `ok` and `severity` unchanged on every branch, so the no-behaviour-change claim is visible in the diff itself; leaving `severity: 'info'` alone is flagged rather than done, which is the right call for something this card was not graded for.

Test quality is the part I'd normally push back on and don't need to: the assertions are **properties, not literals** (names the package, states an origin, is not the retired bare-mount form), and there is a **contrast control** — ragflow's plugin is built here, so its hint must stay the plain mount line. Without that control the first assertion would be satisfied by blanket-rewording every hint in the file. That is exactly the anti-tautology shape this lane keeps having to ask for.

### ⛔ Why this is not a flip yet

**CI is still converging** — 28 checks on `7372c21015`, zero failures so far, most still running. Per this shift's own scar (#10950's ACCEPT declared "zero failures" and a real failure landed minutes later, corrected in `5385444895`), a landing verdict now would be a statement I cannot support. Green is read **by job name**, never off the aggregator, and only once the run finishes.

One gate is also outstanding by the dev's own account: `check:type-check-debt`, the 19th of the derived union, needs the whole workspace closure built and was still running at PR-open time. **`PREREQUISITE NOT MET` is NOT MEASURED and never a pass** — I need its real verdict before flipping.

So: substance ACCEPT, PR stays draft, flip and enqueue on green + that verdict.

**Clause-②: no** — confirmed against the landed diff, not just the plan. A runtime message string and a doc comment in `service-settings`, plus tests. No accept/reject behaviour moves, no public surface widens.

### Sibling finding

#11318 was filed out of this work: `ai.manifest.ts` prints the same un-followable mount instruction for `@objectstack/service-ai`, which `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` declares `edition: 'cloud'`. Correctly filed rather than ridden along.

## Landing verdict — PR #11319 flipped ready and enqueued

The gating condition from my review (`5385612616`) is met. CI on `7372c21015`, read **by job name**, not off an aggregator:

**31 checks, all completed, zero failures.** All six `Test Core` shards, all three `Dogfood Regression Gate` shards, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Build Core`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Check Changeset`, and all four Type Check lanes green. `Console Pin Gate` and `Build Docs` skipped by their own filters.

The one item I was explicitly holding for — **`Type Check · debt ledger`** — passed. That is the CI form of `check:type-check-debt`, the 19th gate of the derived union that the dev reported as still running at PR-open time. CI running it is stronger evidence than a local run, so the "`PREREQUISITE NOT MET` is NOT MEASURED" concern is discharged by measurement rather than waived.

State at flip: `draft: false`, `mergeable_state: clean`, head `7372c21015` unchanged since review, 1 commit, 3 files. Enqueued through the merge queue — not merged directly, not bypassed.

`Fixes #10920` will close this card on merge. That is correct: the in-repo scope of the finding is fully repaired, the `packages/spec` half was fenced out by triage and stays out, and the sibling case is separately on record as #11318.

### What this card ends up having established, beyond its own repair

The finding was filed as "a manifest names a package this repo does not build". The measurement turned it into something more useful: the package **is** published (`latest` 6.9.0), and it is **not co-installable with this platform version** — 6.9.0 exact-pins `@objectstack/spec@6.9.0` against this repo's 17.2.0, so mounting it resolves a second spec rather than reusing this one. The operator was not merely being told to install something unfindable; they were being pointed at a real package that would fail in a confusing way. The shipped message now carries its own version boundary instead of just a package name.

⚠️ And one methodological result worth keeping, because it will recur: **absence from a roster is not a negative answer when the roster was never in the business of listing that kind of thing.** `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` is keyed by platform *service* capability tokens and contains no knowledge adapter at all — not the out-of-repo one, and not the two this repo does build. My dispatch's fork clause told the dev to read that silence as "ships nowhere" and drop the adapter option; the dev measured against the actual source of truth instead. The next card routed through that roster should check whether the roster has a category for the question before treating its silence as evidence.

**Surprises, for the record** (not in the JSON above because they are about the dispatch rather than the code):

1. The dispatch's second fork — *roster present and does not name it ⇒ ships nowhere ⇒ drop the `turso` option* — does not hold, because `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` was never in the business of listing knowledge adapters. Following it would have deleted a published, working adapter. The PM has already recorded this publicly as a defect in the dispatch rather than in execution.
2. The GitHub body sanitizer ate a `<name>` placeholder inside backticks in PR #11319's body, so the documented probe command there now reads `.../@objectstack%2F` with the placeholder missing. ⚠️ I have **not** edited the PR body: the PR is flipped ready and enqueued, and its state is the PM's. The corrected spelling is `@objectstack%2FPACKAGE` — the PM's call whether it is worth a body edit.
3. `pnpm install` rejects `--workspace-concurrency` in pnpm 10.31.0 (`ERROR Unknown option`), unlike `pnpm build`/`pnpm test`. Only the run flavours take it.
